defects.summary: The comment-start fix is half done: `_COMMENT_OPENS_AFTER` omits `)`, which bash treats as a word delimiter exactly like the `;`, `&`, `|`, `(` the fix added. The result is the very false red f2fe649 claims to have closed, at 37 and 102 tests, on `bash -n`-clean shell that runs identically - and the docstring the fix wrote now asserts completeness that is false.
defects.evidence: Bash's rule measured directly at HEAD: `case "$v" in fresh)# the esac below is prose and so is this ;;` runs the arm (prints QUIET, rc=0), and `(echo sub)# a subshell whose esac and ;; are prose` runs the subshell and prints `sub` - so `#` after a closing `)` opens a comment. Three live reproductions, each spliced into .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml, each `bash -n` rc=0 and each producing byte-identical runtime output to pristine for every verdict tested: (a) `fresh|unavailable|"$drift")# quiet on purpose; the ;; and esac here are prose` -> 37 failed, 157 passed, message `an arm of the audit step's case has no pattern this test can read`; (b) `(:)# a subshell whose esac and ;; are prose` in the quiet arm body -> 37 failed, 157 passed, message `no catch-all arm: a status this repo has never heard of matches nothing, says nothing, and the run goes green` with `assert '*' in {'fresh','missing','not-yet-bootstrapped','stale','unavailable','unreadable'}` - i.e. the scanner falsely accuses production of a dead catch-all; (c) the same comment after an arithmetic `))` reproduces (b) identically. Symptom 2 of V2-2 is also still live: splicing `(:)# the heredoc ends with ) || verdict="" and then dispatches` above the real `verdict=$(` line (`bash -n` rc=0) relocates `_tail()` to a slice starting `" and then dispatches\nverdict=$(python3 - <<'PY'...` -> 102 failed, 92 passed. The `|` decoy is covered; `)` is not, and test_the_tail_slice_is_not_relocated_by_a_comment's four decoys are `""`, `: ;`, `true &`, `(`. The fix report justifies excluding `)` with `x=$(echo hi)#notcomment` printing `hi#notcomment` - I reproduced that, but it is the command-substitution `)`, which is part of a word; it says nothing about a subshell, arithmetic or case-pattern `)`. Two false prose claims ride on the gap: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:206 `COMMENTS OPEN WHERE BASH OPENS THEM, which is _COMMENT_OPENS_AFTER and not merely after whitespace` (false - `)` is missing and the `WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MODEL` list below does not name it), and :2160 `THE DECOY IN EVERY SHAPE A COMMENT CAN OPEN IN` (false - two shapes short). Negative control that the added half is real: narrowing `_COMMENT_OPENS_AFTER` back to `" \t\n"` reds 6 tests (3 `_ARMS_OK` shapes + the 3 decoys), so the `;&|(` work is wired; only `)` is missing.

defects.summary: `_ARMS_OK`'s banner claim - "EVERY ONE OF THESE IS VALID BASH THAT SAYS EXACTLY WHAT THE SHIPPED BLOCK SAYS" - is false for at least two fixtures that change control flow, and nothing asserts it. `bash -n` is the only gate, so semantic divergence in a fixture is invisible.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:608 (and the same claim restated in test_a_reformat_bash_cannot_see_does_not_red_this_test's docstring: "Every block here is bash-identical to the shipped one"). I executed all 27 fixtures in real bash against every status in `sel.KNOWN_STATUSES | {UNAVAILABLE}` plus `brand-new`, `""`, `*`, `a b`, crossed with results_ok=yes/no, and diffed stdout+stderr+rc against the control block. `continue-testing-terminator` (:658, `;;&` on the quiet arm) and `fallthrough-terminator` (:660, `;&`) both DIVERGE: verdict `fresh` produces no output on the shipped block and `::warning::the published account audit reads 'fresh', which is not a status this repo knows.` on the fixture - i.e. the fixture makes the happy path annotate, the exact failure the shipped block exists to avoid. (`nested-case-one-line-last-arm` and `command-substitution-in-an-arm-body` also diverge, by replacing/adding output; the remaining divergences are deliberate message-text edits and read fairly under the claim.) The gate in `_bash_n` only runs `bash -n`, so nothing in the suite would notice a fixture that stops meaning what the shipped block means - which is what would let a future "reformat" fixture certify a real behaviour change as invisible.

defects.summary: `_splice`'s replacement rationale (written to close V3-6) promises a failure message it does not deliver: a fixture that drifts from the step reds at import with a bare `AssertionError` naming a string - which is the exact failure mode the same paragraph condemns four sentences later.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:548: "`_ARMS_OK[\"control\"]` runs the full status assertion over `_ARMS_BASE` itself, so a fixture that drifts from the step reds with the drift message rather than passing." Measured: dropping `unreadable` from `_ARMS_BASE` - the report's own cited measurement - does not red with the drift message. It reds at collection: `!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!` / `E AssertionError: case "$verdict" in`, thrown by `_arm`'s `assert _ARMS_BASE.count(old) == count`. Every part of `_ARMS_BASE` is anchored by an `_arm` call (`_QUIET`, `_LIVENESS`, `_CATCHALL`, the two arm patterns), so ANY vocabulary drift in it trips that assert first and the drift message is unreachable. The safety direction holds (it reds rather than passing), but :555-566 of the same docstring argues that a harness failing "with a bare `ValueError` naming a string" is unacceptable because it "says nothing about the workflow" - and that is precisely what this path produces.

defects.summary: Two catch-all spellings that bash treats as genuine catch-alls still red with the expensive misdiagnosis, and one of them (`''|*)`) is named in `_shell_scan`'s docstring as a shape the helper handles better than `shlex`.
defects.evidence: Measured at HEAD, each spliced into the real body, each `bash -n` clean and each producing output byte-identical to the control for an unknown verdict: `''|*)` -> literals gain an empty string, so the set comparison fails and the test reds with "the `case` and account_zip_selection.py disagree about which statuses exist" - the cross-repo drift accusation this whole file exists to eliminate, on a pattern that matches exactly what `*)` matches. `""*)` and `*'')` -> `_unquote` leaves them intact (asymmetric quotes), the token compares unequal to `*`, and the test reds "no catch-all arm". scripts/test_account_workflows.py:244 cites `''|*)` by name as an example of a case pattern `shlex` cannot read, which reads as a claim that this scanner can. Safe direction (loud, not silent green) and exotic shapes, hence nit - but the message points at the wrong file, which is the cost the branch is trying to remove.
